- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (0–7 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model tends to underreact — forecasts remain too high, missing sharp downward corrections.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >40.0), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days, then gradually corrects — use a 7-day moving average to smooth out overcorrection.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 40.0 followed by drop), model should reduce forecast slope by 15–20% in next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model tends to overforecast — apply a 5–10% downward bias if sentiment > 0.5 and price > 40.0.  
- For 14–30 day horizon, model often underestimates volatility — add 2–5% upward bias if sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more) and price is near 38–42.  
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to anticipate — apply a 10–15% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative within 3 days of peak.
